description: Dear Residents and Fellows, Patient Care Fund Application – Due Friday, 9/25/26 In partnership with (and funded through!) UCSF Health and the Office of Graduate Medical Education (GME), we are pleased to announce this year's Patient Care Fund (PCF) call for applications! The PCF seeks proposals from and led by trainees that will improve the quality of patient care at UCSF. Applications are reviewed using the following criteria: Patient Care Impact: Only projects focused on improving tangible care for UCSF Health patients will be funded. Projects will be assessed for relative direct impact and relative long-term benefits to the patient population. Sustainability & Continuity: The proposal will be reviewed based on the potential for ongoing sustainable improvement for patients. If applicable, the proposal should demonstrate the source of ongoing funding necessary to sustain the project long term. Projects with sustained benefits to patients will be given a higher priority. Repeat proposals for projects that have been previously funded will not be considered. [Pilot, longevity] Budget Criteria: Funds are not intended to provide research, staffing, salary support, entertainment expenses, or other expenses inconsistent with UCSF Health or UCSF campus policies. Projects involving educational materials must also include a Patient Education Committee review and Interpreting and Translation Services if translations are needed (and highly suggested for more inclusive patient outreach). Examples of past funded proposals: Children’s books for pediatric clinic waiting areasPediatric hygiene kits to provide hair care items to patients with curly or coiled hairEducational pamphlets, magnets, and posters for pediatric or birthing patients"CARE" carts with medical resources, games, and art for geriatric inpatient unitsIndividualized patient gowns for breast cancer patients coming for multiple weekly radiation therapyArt supplies for a pediatrics art day event or art kits for geriatric / pediatric patientsLiveWell comics for pediatric patients with Irritable Bowel DiseaseTake-home culturally congruent cookbooks for discharge medicine patientsTake-home sunscreen / moisturizer kit for dermatology patientsProposals are due: Friday, September 26, 2025 Application Link: UCSF Patient Care Fund (2026-2027) For more information, see our PCF FAQ or visit our PCF Website. We are committed to improving the quality of patient care at UCSF and are happy to help you develop your idea, so please do not hesitate to reach out to us with any follow-up requests/ questions! Contact: Marisa McFarlane (marisa.mcfarlane@ucsf.edu)

description: San Francisco’s free outdoor movie tradition is back with a full season for 2026. The Sundown Cinema series has just announced its lineup, bringing family-friendly films to parks across the city from June through October. All screenings are free and open to the public, with movies beginning around sunset. The events typically draw large crowds, so arriving early is recommended to secure a good spot. Guests are welcome to bring blankets and low-back chairs, and outside food and drinks are generally permitted, subject to park rules. Attendees can RSVP in advance for a chance to win access to a reserved seating section near the screen. One lucky winner at each screening will also receive their Amazon Wish List, valued up to $1,000. description: Hands-on Pain Education (HOPE) is a dynamic, two-day course designed for practicing clinicians looking to elevate their pain management skills through an experiential, hands-on approach. Led by Noigroup Director Luke Bongiorno, the course integrates modern pain science with practical manual therapy, active pain education, exposure strategies, emotional regulation, and breathing techniques. Clinicians will gain a deeper understanding of the multidimensional nature of pain while developing immediately applicable tools to assess, modulate, and treat pain more effectively in clinical practice. Presented by Luke Bongiorno of HOPE. Hosted by the UCSF Department of Physical Therapy and Rehabilitation Sciences.

description: Session Overview This hands-on workshop focuses on how to best start basic literature searching using a combination of databases, search engines, and AI tools. Discussion will cover questions to consider that guide whether an AI tool, such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Consensus, and Perplexity, can be helpful in the literature searching process. Participants will practice searching a combination of databases, search engines, and AI tools to critique the results. There will be time for questions and discussion throughout the workshop. description: Osher WISE Course: What Should I Take? Making Informed Choices About Dietary Supplements and Herbal Medicine Wednesdays, October 7–28, 6:00-7:30 p.m. PT Approximately 1 in 5 adults uses a plant-based herbal supplement, and 1 in 2 uses a vitamin or mineral product. Many people do not tell their health care providers about the supplements they are taking. This communication gap can increase the risk of interactions with prescription medications, existing health conditions, and other treatments. As the use of dietary supplements continues to grow, it is important for people to understand how to evaluate these products, recognize their potential benefits and risks, and identify which supplements are supported by strong scientific evidence. Accessing reliable, evidence-based information can help everyone make safer, more informed decisions about their health. This four-week course will help participants learn essential tips for dietary supplement selection and evidence-based information on the effectiveness and potential risks for supplements and herbals commonly used for longevity, heart health, bone health, and other uses. This course is chaired by UCSF Clinical Pharmacy Faculty, Dr. Candy Tsourounis and Dr. Cathi Dennehy. October 7: Dietary Supplements and Herbal Medicine Essentials: What You Need to Know October 14: Supplements for Healthy Aging: What's Popular, and Should I Take It? October 21: Longevity: Can Supplements Help You Live Longer and Healthier? October 28: Vitamins and Minerals: What Makes Sense for You Register here Our educational programming, formerly known as Osher Mini Medical School for the Public, has been reimagined as Osher WISE (Well-being and Integrative Science for Everyone). This public education program offers courses on integrative health topics that are current and compelling, providing an opportunity for community members to become active, informed participants in their own journey to health and well-being. https://osher.ucsf.edu/Osher-WISE, powered by Localist, the Community Event Platform
